A 19th-century academic oil painting with a smooth, finely blended surface: soft glazed transitions, delicate fine detail, minimal visible brushstrokes, no heavy impasto, no rough texture. Strong light and shadow from a single warm source (a lamp, a torch, a fire, a low sun) or from heavy overcast, with deep chiaroscuro. Palette of umber, ochre, gold, olive and near-black, with occasional cool accents. The manner of a romantic landscape, a grand historical scene, or a natural-history study of a creature painted as if real. A low, close viewpoint. Wet, reflective stone where there is stone; ancient architecture where there is architecture; one saturated subject held against darkness; scale shown by something small beside something vast. Quiet, watchful, ominous mood. No text, no lettering, no border, no frame, no grid texture, not photographic.

A single figure standing still on a worn earth track in very old forest, at evening in autumn after rain, seen from low on the track a few paces behind the figure, so that its back is to the viewer and its head is in deep shadow, with no face and no hair to be made out. A thin, patient person of no particular age. Human-seeming. Pale hands that are always a little damp. Barefoot, always. Undyed linen: a loose shirt and trousers, worn soft, washed many times. A plain cloth bag over one shoulder. In it: seed in twists of cloth, a small sealed clay crock, a short knife with a bone handle. Small fungi come up wherever it rests for long. No look of rank. When it listens through the ground it sits or kneels where it is with bare hands or feet in the soil, unseeing. Here it has only this moment arrived, so no fungi have come up at its feet, and it is not listening: it stands upright with its hands at its sides and the bag closed, small beneath the trees. The track is trodden earth, wet and dark, wide enough for two people to walk abreast, running away ahead of the figure between the trunks until the trees close over it. Beside the track there are coppiced stools and cut stumps. The trees are very large and very old; fallen ones lie where they fell, with young growth coming up through them; fungi grow everywhere, on the logs and through the deep wet leaf litter. To one side a rib of pale rock breaks the ground, slick with rain, and beyond it lies a sinkhole among the roots with dark water standing at the bottom. The only light is the last grey light of a heavy overcast that is breaking up, coming down through one gap in the canopy onto the figure's linen, the wet track and the pale rock; everything else falls away to near-black. In that gap, high overhead between the breaking clouds, there is one small, steady, pale blue point of light. No other figures, no animals, no buildings, no smoke. The small figure beneath the great trunks gives the scale.
